title: Provision-to-ready: customer impact statement + comms guidance for Dedicated provisioning improvements
creator: Irene Choi
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
## Context
Infra/SRE/Platform are shipping “provision-to-ready” automation for Dedicated capacity. This will reduce time-to-ready for new Dedicated pools and expansions by standardizing golden images, automating orchestration, and enforcing validation gates.

This ticket defines what we can promise externally, the customer-facing value proposition, and internal guidance for Sales/CS/Support/Field engineering.

---

## Goals
1) Define customer-facing impact (what improves, for whom, and when).
2) Set expectations: what we will NOT promise (avoid over-committing to absolute provisioning times).
3) Provide messaging + FAQ for:
   - Dedicated new pool bring-up
   - Dedicated expansions (adding nodes)
   - Readiness states and “Validating/Quarantined” behavior
4) Align on comms surfaces (release notes, enablement, support macros) and owners.

---

## Customer-facing impact (approved messaging)
### What’s improving
- **Faster time-to-ready for Dedicated capacity and expansions** via automated provisioning + validated readiness gates.
- **Higher predictability**: fewer manual steps, fewer “surprise” failures after the pool is reported online.
- **Better transparency for operators**: readiness state and a basic failure reason will be available to Redwood internal tooling; customer-facing visibility may be limited initially.

### Who benefits
- Customers on **Redwood Dedicated** who:
  - Provision new pools
  - Expand existing pools
  - Operate in regions/GPU SKUs included in the staged rollout

### What we will say externally (safe promise)
- “We’re investing in automation that reduces the time it takes to bring new Dedicated capacity online and improves the consistency of bring-up across regions/GPU types.”
- “Our system now validates GPU health, driver/toolkit parity, networking, and a lightweight workload canary before capacity is marked ready.”
- “This reduces the likelihood of late failures and shortens the time between capacity allocation and being ready to serve production traffic.”

### What we will NOT promise (explicitly)
- No guaranteed absolute provisioning time for all customers/regions/SKUs (unless already contracted in a bespoke SOW).
- No claim that quarantine will never happen; quarantine is an explicit safety mechanism.
- No claim that “Ready” means “optimal performance”—only that the node passed baseline checks and a smoke canary.
- No promise of customer-visible step-by-step logs in the first release (internal-only initially).

---

## Proposed external positioning (copy blocks)
### Short release-note blurb (public-safe)
“Improved Dedicated capacity bring-up: Redwood has added automated provisioning and validation for Dedicated GPU nodes, reducing time-to-ready and helping ensure capacity is healthy before it serves traffic.”

### Sales deck / customer email (longer)
“We’ve introduced an automated provision-to-ready workflow for Dedicated capacity. Nodes now move through standardized image provisioning and a set of health/compatibility checks (GPU health, driver parity, networking, and a workload smoke canary) before they’re counted as ready capacity. This reduces manual intervention during expansions, improves predictability across regions, and lowers the risk of late-stage failures impacting your ramp.”

---

## FAQ (for Sales/CS/Support)
### Q: Does this change how customers request Dedicated capacity?
A: No. The commercial process and capacity request flow are unchanged. The improvement is in the internal bring-up pipeline after capacity is allocated.

### Q: What does “Ready” mean now?
A: “Ready” means the node has joined the cluster and passed required validation gates (hardware/driver/network + smoke canary) and is eligible to join the serving pool.

### Q: What happens if a node fails validation?
A: It will either be retried (bounded retries) or **quarantined** depending on the failure class. Quarantined nodes do not serve traffic. Operators may reimage or replace.

### Q: Can this reduce available capacity (due to quarantine)?
A: In rare cases, yes—quarantine is intended to prevent unhealthy nodes from degrading latency or causing incidents. If quarantine rates threaten capacity targets, Infra/SRE will tune thresholds and/or fast-track remediations.

### Q: Will customers see the validation failure reason?
A: Not initially in a self-serve UI. Support can share high-level cause categories (e.g., driver mismatch, GPU health check failure, NCCL fabric issue) when it helps troubleshooting.

### Q: Is there a behavior change during high demand (capacity tight)?
A: Capacity will not be counted as ready until validations pass. This is a reliability guardrail; we prefer temporarily slower ramp over bringing unhealthy capacity online.

---

## Internal comms guidance
### Support macro (internal)
- Acknowledge request and share that “Dedicated expansions go through automated readiness validation.”
- Ask for: pool ID, region, GPU type, timestamps, and whether any recent pool image channel changes occurred.
- Provide expectation: “Bring-up time varies; our system will only mark capacity ready after health checks. If nodes are stuck validating/quarantined, we can investigate and may reimage/replace.”
- Escalation triggers:
  - Validating > 60 minutes for multiple nodes
  - Quarantine rate > 10% of expansion batch
  - Customer reports capacity shortfall affecting prod traffic

### Sales/CS enablement notes
- Don’t quote fixed times. Use “reduces time-to-ready” and “improves predictability.”
- If pressed for numbers: route to SRE/Infra for region/SKU-specific historical ranges and note these are not guarantees.

---

## Comms plan + surfaces
- Internal (must-have):
  - #eng-infra + #eng-sre weekly updates during rollout
  - Support macro + escalation rules (CS Ops)
  - Sales/CS enablement snippet for Dedicated expansions (GTM enablement)
- External (optional / phased):
  - Public release notes line item once rollout is stable in at least one region/SKU
  - 1:many email to affected Dedicated customers only if the improvement is material and broadly rolled out

Owners:
- PM (this ticket): messaging, FAQ, release note draft
- Infra/SRE: provide baseline → post-change metrics for internal confidence; approve any numbers shared
- Support Ops: macro + routing
- Sales enablement: internal snippet and “what not to promise” guidance

---

## Metrics & claims policy
- External claims must be qualitative unless explicitly approved by SRE + Infra leadership.
- Any quantitative claim must specify scope (region, GPU type, new pool vs expansion) and be based on post-rollout data.
